policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 5 Jan close (1x4 3.79, 3x6 3.55, 6x9 3.36, 9x12 3.32 vs WIBOR 3M 3.95) price roughly 65bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The NBP survey of professional forecasters (2 Jan) sees an average reference rate of 3.69% in 2026. Credit Agricole (5 Jan): the market prices three incomplete cuts by end-2026; Erste/Santander (5 Jan) expects a hold for a while, then cuts in March and May.
policy.risk_text: MPC members ruled out a January cut (Kotecki 10 Dec; Wnorowski and Kotecki 16 Dec: no change at the next two meetings). If cuts are pushed out, front-end roll-down does not materialise; Santander (9 Dec) expected higher short-end yields in Q1 as cut expectations are repriced.

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 3.7% (2025), 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); December 2025 flash CPI 2.4% y/y.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~6.9% of GDP (MoF plan); 2026 budget deficit cap PLN 271.7bn, gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn; Santander (19 Dec) noted the 10Y ASW back near 100bp on global fiscal worries.
macro.fiscal_risk_text: Q1 2026 supply of PLN 75-100bn over 8 auctions; Fitch (27 Feb) and Moody's (20 Mar) reviews with negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut six times in 2025 to 4.00% (last on 3 Dec); CPI fell to 2.4% in December (flash, 31 Dec; final on 15 Jan, core estimated ~2.8% by Erste), the NBP projects 2.9% for 2026 (professional forecasters, 2 Jan: 2.6%). Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.5 in December (2 Jan). GDP grew 3.8% y/y in Q3. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. Since 2 Jan: bank dailies (5 Jan) expect POLGBs to keep their relative strength after the sub-target December CPI (PKO), with IRS 2Y/5Y/10Y down 6-7bp in the week to 2 Jan (Credit Agricole). 6 Jan was a Polish holiday; abroad, US ISM manufacturing fell to 47.9 (5 Jan; 48.4 expected) and German December CPI surprised lower (1.8% y/y, HICP 2.0%; 6 Jan). Venezuela after the 3 Jan US operation was shrugged off by markets; the 6 Jan Paris declaration on Ukraine has the UK and France pledging troops after a ceasefire. Street views (December): PKO 1Q26 forecast 2Y 3.75 / 5Y 4.50 / 10Y 5.10; Santander expects higher yields in Q1 on supply and cut repricing; ING says early-2026 trading follows MoF's Q1 issuance.

calendar.plan_text: MoF Q1 2026 financing plan (31 Dec 2025): 8 sale auctions for PLN 75-100bn, one switch auction, possible foreign issuance. January: sale auctions on 9 Jan (PLN 7-12bn), 22 Jan (8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); no switch auction in January; 36-week T-bill auction on 16 Jan (PLN 2-4bn). 2026 gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn. BGK: FPC to issue domestically in 2026 (up to PLN 18.5bn). Series for the 9 Jan auction had not been announced by 6 Jan.
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug 2025-Jan 2026 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction (rally regime) and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (9, 22, 28 Jan) rather than the day before. January supply is front-loaded (PLN 22-37bn across three auctions) after only ~21-23% pre-financing. For the front end the 13-14 Jan MPC is the event: members pre-announced no January cut, so a hold is the base case; the December final CPI (15 Jan) and the February/March meetings drive the cut timing.
